name: WPConvert Developer API
description:
The WPConvert Developer API converts a zipped frontend project (static HTML, or a build output from tools such as Lovable, v0, Bolt, Cursor, Replit, or Framer) into an installable WordPress theme.

## Versioning

`info.version` is the version of this API **document**, not of the developer tooling. The published CLI (`wpconvert`) and MCP server (`@wpconvert/mcp`) are versioned independently and are currently at `0.3.0`.

## Typical flow

1. `GET /api/convert/quota` — preflight. Read `capabilities.conversion` to
   learn whether a conversion may start and what it will consume.
2. Submit the project: `POST /api/convert` for archives up to the multipart
   ceiling, or the signed-upload flow (`POST /api/convert/upload-url`, an
   external `PUT`, then `POST /api/convert/from-storage`) for larger inputs.
3. Poll `GET /api/convert/{jobId}/status` until `status` is `done` or `failed`. 4. On success, call `GET /api/download/{projectId}` for a short-lived signed
   theme URL, and/or `POST /api/playground/sessions` for an in-browser
   WordPress Playground preview.


## Conversion modes

A submission resolves to one of two modes, reported as `conversion_mode`:

- `full` — a downloadable theme. Requires Pro/Agency entitlement or credits. - `preview_only` — a free developer preview. Previewable in Playground but
  **never downloadable**, even after a later upgrade. Running a paid
  conversion again is required to obtain a downloadable artifact.


Use `capabilities.conversion.mode` from the quota endpoint to determine which mode the next submission will use.

## Response envelope variance

This API predates a unified error envelope, and the current production behavior is deliberately documented as-is rather than normalized. API-key requests usually receive `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`, but several endpoints still emit legacy flat shapes. Operations that can return more than one shape model that with `oneOf`. Branch on the HTTP status first, then on `error.code` when the nested object is present.

## Operational limits

The values below are the current production defaults. They are environment-configurable and may change without a change to this document. The stable part of the contract is the error **code** and response behavior, not the exact counts.

| Limit | Current default | | --- | --- | | Conversion submissions (standard API key) | 3/min, 20/hour | | Conversion submissions (preview-only entitlement) | 2/min, 5/hour | | Status polling | 30/min | | Concurrent in-flight conversions | Agency 3, Pro 2, PAYG 1, preview-only 1 | | Signed upload URL creation | 20 per 10 minutes | | Playground sessions | 10/hour |

Exceeding a throttle returns `rate_limited`; exceeding the concurrency cap returns `too_many_active_jobs`.
